texts.full_text: a hybrid protein between and tumor necrosis factor-beta. A hybrid protein between interferon-gamma and tumor necrosis factor-beta was made by ligating the respective genes and expressing the fused genes under the control of the trp promoter in Escherichia coli. The fusion proteins were purified using affinity chromatography on a Ni-NTA column followed by size exclusion gel filtration to remove aggregates. The antiproliferative activity was assessed through several assays including cell viability, proliferation and apoptosis induction in various cancer cells. The hybrid protein showed significant inhibitory effects against the growth of certain tumor types compared with either interferon-gamma or tumour necrosis factor-beta alone when tested at similar concentrations. The underlying mechanism for this enhanced antiproliferative activity was investigated through examining intracellular signaling pathways, gene expression profiles and cytokine production. The results indicated that unlike the parent proteins which act primarily on specific cell surface receptors (such as interferon gamma receptor or tumor necrosis factor beta受体), these hybrid molecules may induce a more complex cellular response involving multiple signal transduction routes. Furthermore it was observed in some cases, this protein had better stability and longer half-life compared to its individual components due possibly because of the stabilization effect from fusion partner. This might contribute towards improving therapeutic efficacy by providing sustained exposure at effective concentrations within targeted tissues or tumors for a more prolonged duration without increasing toxicity which is often an issue with high doses. texts.full_text: date information about the potential employee. The Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) has, for the past forty years, employed regulatory policies that govern primarily who have access to your information and how that information might be used. It basically requires that the CRAs: Limit access to your information Give your consent before providing your information to the employer Investigate disputed information Correct/delete inaccurate information Delete outdated information Disclose your credit file and information upon request Rise in errors by some of the biggest CRAs, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) have tightened rules over the human resourcing industry. The FTC has brought several actions against the background check companies for failing to ensure accuracy. The most notable one was against HireRight Solutions Inc., a company that provides pre-employment screening services, including criminal history reports, for $2.6 million in 2013 (FTC v. Hire Right). Another case involved General Information Services Inc. which paid out over $2.96 million to the FTC for failing to follow reasonable procedures when reporting public record information on job applicants. The CFPB also brought an action against one of the largest CRAs, Experian and its subsidiaries for allegedly including erroneous data in consumer reports, violating federal law by misrepresenting credit scores provided to consumers as being the same ones lenders used to make loan decisions.
